newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: U.S. author apologises to Portuguese airline.
newsitem.headline: U.S. author apologises to Portuguese airline.

text.p: Top-selling U.S. author Michael Crichton has apologised to the Portuguese airline TAP over a reference to a company he calls "Air Portugal" in his latest thriller, an airline spokeswoman said on Thursday.

Crichton, whose successes include "Jurassic Park", wrote in "Airframe", his latest blockbuster about a mysterious 10,000-metre plunge of a plane, that maintenance at Air Portugal was "so inept" that it almost caused a serious accident.
TAP-Air Portugal is the full name of the Portuguese state airline.
"A fax arrived at TAP this week expressing apologies. A copy of the fax has been handed over to a lawyer who will review the matter," TAP spokeswoman Isabel Palma told Reuters.

The Diario de Noticias newspaper reported on Thursday that Crichton had promised to correct the reference in future editions of his thriller. The TAP spokeswoman was unable immediately to confirm the report.
TAP said last week it might sue Crichton over the thriller. Company chairman Manuel Ferreira Lima said TAP had turned the matter over to a leading Portuguese lawyer for an opinion.
TAP recently reached an accord with Air France under which the two airlines will exchange maintenance contracts.
